keywords: 三种策略基类有什么区别
每只股票用不同参数怎么设
title: Three strategy base classes and per-share parameters
summary: Pick RuleIterator (timing rules), FactorSorter (cross-section rank), or GeneralStg (flexible shapes). Per-share parameter maps use share codes as keys (optional default)—that map is not a signal type.
narrative:
Custom strategies usually inherit one of three bases:

- RuleIterator: single-rule or single-share timing loops (moving-average style). Output is often a scalar or 1-D position-like signal.
- FactorSorter: score many shares on a factor, then keep top/bottom N (max_sel_count, sort_ascending).
- GeneralStg: flexible multi-asset or multi-rule shapes when the first two do not fit.

Per-share parameters: after set_shares, pass a mapping {share_code: parameter_tuple, ...} via update_par_values or Operator.set_parameter(..., par_values=...). Keys must match share strings exactly. An optional "default" key supplies the tuple for shares not listed—there is no others / rest magic key. A plain tuple at init means one shared parameter set for all shares. That per-share mapping is a parameter table, not a signal type and not set_parameter(..., pars={parameter_name: value}).

This card may sketch return shapes. Parameter declarations, data windows, and get_data / get_pars contracts belong to the realize card. What PT / PS / VS numbers mean belongs to the signal-types card.
risk_notes: Per-share dict keys are share codes. Do not confuse them with PT target-weight signals or with pars={name: value}.
